cues.caption: Hello, champ! Welcome to class
cues.text: Hello, champ! Welcome back to Mentr Learn. I am so happy you are here today.

cues.caption: Unit 1 · How Computers Work
cues.text: Today we start Computer Science — Unit one — How Computers Work.

cues.caption: Chapter 1 · What Is a Computer?
cues.text: This is Chapter one. The name of our lesson is: What Is a Computer?

cues.caption: Say with me: What Is a Computer?
cues.text: Say the title with me, nice and slow… What… Is… A… Computer?

cues.caption: Great! Let's begin
cues.text: Great! Keep that title in your mind. Ready? Let's go.

cues.caption: So many machines at home…
cues.text: Look around your home. Phones, TVs, fans, toasters, lamps… so many machines!

cues.caption: Are ALL of them computers?
cues.text: But wait. Are all of them computers? Hmm. What do you think?

cues.caption: ⏸ Your turn — point to a computer!
cues.text: Pause and think for a moment. Point to one thing near you that you think is a computer.

cues.caption: Good thinking! We'll check soon
cues.text: Good thinking! We will check your answer together at the end.

cues.caption: Secret: a computer has 3 jobs
cues.text: Here is the big secret. A computer is a special machine with three jobs.

cues.caption: 1 · INPUT = something goes in
cues.text: Job one — INPUT. That means something goes in.

cues.caption: 2 · PROCESS = it thinks / works
cues.text: Job two — PROCESS. That means the machine thinks, or works on it.

cues.caption: 3 · OUTPUT = something comes out
cues.text: Job three — OUTPUT. That means something comes out — an answer, a picture, or a sound.

cues.caption: Say together: Input · Process · Output
cues.text: Let's say the three jobs together: Input… Process… Output!

cues.caption: All 3 jobs → it's a computer
cues.text: Wonderful. If a machine does all three jobs, we can call it a computer.

cues.caption: Story: sending a message
cues.text: Let's try a real story. Imagine you send a message to your friend on a phone.

cues.caption: You type → INPUT
cues.text: First, you type the words with your fingers. That is INPUT — words going in.

cues.caption: Phone works → PROCESS
cues.text: Next, the phone works on your message — it gets it ready to send. That is PROCESS.

cues.caption: Friend sees it → OUTPUT
cues.text: Then your friend sees the message on their screen. That is OUTPUT.

cues.caption: Phone = computer ✓
cues.text: So — input, process, output. Your phone did all three jobs. Your phone is a computer!

cues.caption: Laptop · Phone · Tablet = computers
cues.text: A laptop can do the same. A tablet can do the same. They are computers too.

cues.caption: Story: switching on a bulb
cues.text: Now, another story. You press a switch, and a bulb lights up.

cues.caption: Useful — but is it a computer?
cues.text: The switch sends power. The bulb gets hot and shines. That is useful!

cues.caption: No real “thinking” like a computer
cues.text: But the bulb is not taking many kinds of input and thinking about a message or a game.

cues.caption: Bulb · Toaster → NOT computers
cues.text: It mainly turns light on or off. So a simple bulb — or a toaster that only heats bread — is not a computer.

cues.caption: Computers work in a smarter way
cues.text: Remember: computers take input, process it, and show output in a smarter way.

cues.caption: Game: say YES or NO!
cues.text: Quick game time! I will name something. You say YES if it is a computer, or NO if it is not.

cues.caption: Laptop → YES ✓
cues.text: Ready? Laptop… Yes! A laptop is a computer.

cues.caption: Phone → YES ✓
cues.text: Phone… Yes! A phone is a computer.

cues.caption: Tablet → YES ✓
cues.text: Tablet… Yes! A tablet is a computer.

cues.caption: Toaster → NO ✗
cues.text: Toaster… No! A toaster is not a computer — it only heats bread.

cues.caption: Lamp → NO ✗
cues.text: Lamp… No! A lamp is not a computer.

cues.caption: High five! You're amazing 🙌
cues.text: You are doing amazing. High five!

cues.caption: Practice check question
cues.text: One more thinking question — the same kind you will see later in your check.

cues.caption: Laptop · Lamp · Bicycle bell — which?
cues.text: Which one is a computer: a laptop, a lamp, or a bicycle bell?

cues.caption: Answer: Laptop ✓
cues.text: If you said laptop — you are right! Because it takes input, processes, and shows output.

cues.caption: Lamp & bell → helpful, not computers
cues.text: A lamp and a bicycle bell are helpful, but they are not computers.

cues.caption: Lock in: Input · Process · Output
cues.text: Let's lock it in. A computer has three jobs: input, process, and output.

cues.caption: Computers vs not-computers
cues.text: Phone, laptop, tablet — computers. Toaster, lamp — not computers.

cues.caption: Chapter 1 complete · Brilliant!
cues.text: You learned Chapter one: What Is a Computer? Brilliant work today!

cues.text: Next, you will play a short quiz to practise. Tap Finish when you are ready. See you there, champ!
